description:
Redwood Inference is running a Reliability Program focused on meeting customer-facing SLOs while scaling the Hosted API’s throughput and reducing incident volume during traffic spikes. The “Hosted circuit breakers + load shedding” project introduces systematic overload protection across the request path (API gateway → routing/control plane → runtime/GPU pools) with two outcomes: (1) prevent cascading failures and tail-latency collapse during overload; (2) return clear, consistent, customer-actionable errors and safe degradation modes instead of ambiguous 5xx timeouts.

Goals:
- Reduce Sev1/Sev2 incidents caused by overload (queue blowups, GPU pool saturation, regional brownouts) by introducing layered circuit breakers and deterministic load-shedding behavior.
- Improve customer experience during overload with stable, documented error semantics (e.g., 429/503 with Redwood-specific error codes), predictable retry guidance (Retry-After), and optional graceful degradation (fallback model/region/tier policies when available).
- Protect core platform stability: cap queue depth, shed early at the edge when possible, avoid retry storms, and maintain control-plane responsiveness.
- Add observability and SLO alignment: new metrics, dashboards, and alerting tied to error budgets and overload signals.

Scope:
- Edge/API gateway: admission control hooks, request classification (tier, route/model, streaming vs non-streaming), error mapping, and headers.
- Routing/control plane: per-(model, region, tier) circuit breaker state, integration with capacity signals, and fallback policy interaction.
- Runtime/data plane: bounded queues, backpressure, shed points at prefill/decode scheduling boundaries, and protection of KV-cache/memory pressure scenarios.
- Customer-facing behavior: error taxonomy, docs updates, console/status-page messaging patterns, and support runbooks.

Non-goals:
- Replacing existing quotas/rate limits (this complements them).
- Major re-architecture of the scheduler; focus is on guardrails and deterministic failure modes.
- Customer-specific bespoke overload logic (support is via configuration/policy primitives).

Key stakeholders:
- SRE & Reliability: Sean Gallagher (SRE Director), Rafael Mendes (SRE Manager), Christine Wong, Tomáš Novák.
- Smart Routing/Platform: Mina Haddad (Eng Manager), Ravi Menon, Elena Popov, Amara Diallo (API gateway), Jordan Lee (policy engine).
- Runtime: Noah Patel, Omar El-Sayed, Lena Fischer, Samir Qureshi.
- Product: Nikhil Sharma (Hosted API), Lauren Bishop (Dedicated—alignment on shared behavior), Henry Cho.
- Observability: Allison Grant, Sergio Costa.

Timeline (approximate):
- Phase 0 (Discovery, 1–2 weeks): analyze top overload failure modes from incidents and metrics; define error taxonomy and target behaviors.
- Phase 1 (Foundations, 3–5 weeks): implement core circuit breaker primitives, bounded queues, and baseline metrics; ship behind feature flags.
- Phase 2 (Policy + Degradation, 3–6 weeks): integrate routing/capacity signals, fallback interactions, and customer-tier aware behaviors.
- Phase 3 (Rollout + Hardening, 2–4 weeks): canary in one region/model, game days, alert tuning, docs/support enablement, expand rollout.

Deliverables:
- Confluence design/ADR set, updated SLO and runbooks, dashboards/alerts, implementation PRs across gateway/routing/runtime, rollout plan, game day artifacts, and support/customer communication templates.

Constraints and risks:
- Avoid retry storms: ensure errors are cacheable/consistent and clients receive explicit retry guidance.
- Prevent breaker flapping: incorporate hysteresis and cool-down periods.
- Preserve fairness across tenants/tiers: align with existing quotas and ensure Dedicated has predictable behavior.
- Maintain compatibility for SDKs/OpenAI-compatible endpoints: consistent error shape and headers across modes.

files.description: Program overview: motivations, target SLO/SLA impacts, phased plan, owners, and success metrics for hosted overload protection.
ADR defining customer-facing overload error semantics (status codes, Redwood error codes, Retry-After guidance, body shape) and compatibility constraints.
ADR specifying breaker state machine (closed/open/half-open), hysteresis/cooldowns, signal inputs, and required telemetry.
Service inventory: which components own admission control, breaker evaluation, capacity signals, and how responsibilities are split across teams.
Updates to SLO definitions/alerts to account for load shedding and to distinguish 'overload-protected' errors from internal failures.
Operational runbook: diagnosing overload, interpreting breaker metrics, safe manual overrides, and rollback steps during an incident.
Game day plan to validate breakers/shedding: scenarios, expected behaviors, monitoring checklist, and pass/fail criteria.
Dashboard spec: key panels (admission rate, shed rate, breaker state, queue depth, p95/p99 latency, 429/503 breakdown by route/model/region).
Support-facing guidance: how to explain overload errors, recommended client retry/backoff patterns, and common misconfigurations.
PRD for customer experience: messaging requirements, documentation updates, API compatibility, and rollout/announcement plan.
Comms template for status page and customer updates when load shedding is active (what to say, what not to say, required metrics).
Observability standard: metric names, labels/cardinality guidance, sampling, and tracing requirements for overload protection.
Initiative umbrella: Hosted circuit breakers + load shedding (goals, milestones, cross-team dependencies, rollout plan).
Implement API gateway admission control hook with tier/route classification and feature flagging.
Add standardized overload error payload + headers (Retry-After) for hosted endpoints, including OpenAI-compat mapping.
Routing: introduce per-(model, region, tier) circuit breaker state store and evaluation API.
Routing: integrate capacity signals (GPU pool saturation, queue depth) into breaker open/close decisions.
Runtime: implement bounded request queues and deterministic shed points (prefill/decode) with explicit reasons.
Runtime: add memory-pressure/KV-cache guardrails to trigger load shedding before OOM/latency spiral.
SRE: define breaker thresholds, hysteresis, and safe default configs per region/model class.
Observability: add metrics + traces for admission decisions, shed reasons, and breaker transitions.
Dashboards: ship overload protection dashboard and initial alert rules aligned to SLOs.
Perf testing: add synthetic overload scenarios to perf-canary and CI gating for regressions.
Docs: update public/internal docs for overload errors and client retry guidance; coordinate with DevEx.
Incident-bot: automatically annotate incidents with breaker state snapshots and key overload metrics.
Rollout: canary in us-east for 1–2 models, evaluate customer impact, then expand globally.
Game day execution ticket: run overload drills, capture findings, and create follow-up tasks.
PM spec alignment: customer-facing behavior during overload, error messaging principles, and deprecation/compat commitments.
Launch planning: customer comms, changelog entry, and support enablement timeline for overload protection rollout.
Console UX: draft how overload events/errors should appear in dashboards and customer-visible analytics (if applicable).
SDKs: surface overload error codes and Retry-After header cleanly in Python/TS/Go SDK error objects.
Dedicated alignment: confirm behavior differences for Dedicated pools (shed behavior, error semantics, SLA considerations).
Policy engine: add guardrails to prevent customers from configuring unsafe fallback/degradation policies.
Edge fairness: ensure admission control respects tenant isolation and avoids starving low-volume tenants.
Alert tuning: reduce noise/flapping by adjusting hysteresis and alert windows once canary data is collected.
Post-launch review: compare incident rate, p99 latency, and customer tickets pre/post rollout; decide next iteration.
PR: API gateway middleware to evaluate admission control and return standardized overload errors with Retry-After.
PR: Add shared error-code enum and JSON schema for Redwood overload responses across REST + OpenAI-compat endpoints.
PR: Routing service circuit breaker state machine implementation with hysteresis and persistence.
PR: Integrate GPU pool capacity signals into routing decisions (breaker inputs + shed hints).
PR: Runtime bounded queue + early shed at scheduler boundary; includes unit tests and perf characterization.
PR: Runtime memory-pressure guardrail to shed before KV-cache thrash/OOM; adds new metrics.
PR: Add overload reason codes end-to-end (gateway→routing→runtime) and plumb through logs/traces.
PR: New Grafana dashboard JSON and alert rules for breaker transitions, shed rate, and queue depth thresholds.
PR: Extend SLO toolkit to track 'overload-protected' errors separately from internal 5xx for error-budget accounting.
PR: Add overload test scenarios (step-function traffic, long-prompt spikes) and gating thresholds for p99 + error mix.
PR: Incident bot enhancement to snapshot breaker states and post a standard overload triage checklist in #incidents.
PR: Python SDK surfaces Retry-After and Redwood overload error codes; adds docs and tests.
PR: TypeScript SDK overload error typing + helper for safe retry/backoff; aligns with API schema.
PR: Go SDK error handling improvements for overload responses; adds examples for exponential backoff with jitter.
PR: Map Redwood overload codes into OpenAI-style error objects without breaking existing client expectations.
PR: Public docs update describing overload errors, recommended retry strategy, and how Dedicated differs from Hosted.
PR: Feature-flagged rollout controls for overload protection (per region/model) and safe default configuration.
